brief: QQQ has held its August 4 range (707.53-725.66) for over a month despite surging crude and rates, but breadth deteriorated: equal-weight QQEW -3%, semis XSD -6.5%, industrials XLI -8.25%, discretionary XLY -5% since the 8/4 close. A close below 702.70 would open an 'island gap,' leaving a month of buyers underwater; that likely requires a firm CPI, with no stated view from the author. A cooler CPI could spark a relief rally with vol down and the market pricing out next week's FOMC hike (~70% odds), but QQQ would still sit inside its 8/4 range with much of the market still vulnerable, so a rally would not change the dynamic. Energy (XLE, +25% QTD) has hedged other market weakness but is losing torque: crude rose over 8% in two days while XLE gained under 50bps, an asymmetric setup, with two downside risks: a correlation-one selloff, or a de-escalation headline unwinding crude sharply. WTI sentiment (DSI 91) is the highest since 9/18/23, after which crude fell 3% in two days, then peaked and fell 30% into December; yet from 9/18/23-10/27/23 crude and SPY fell together, so a crude top isn't always short-term bullish for stocks, though lower crude would help medium-term.
